summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (N23) proposing an assumption-kill experiment to test whether guanfacine retains working memory/attention phenotype when alpha2A-class PFC WM attribution is abolished via genetic LOF or pharmacological antagonism. The document is a research discussion (propose-assay stage), not a completed experiment. It synthesizes existing necessity literature (against residual) and phenotype priors (lacking abolish arms), concluding that the key residual-under-abolish H2H result is currently UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis (N23)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered acute/subacute PFC working memory/attention panel with an alpha2-class positive WM arm, an alpha2A genetic LOF or alpha2-antagonist-matched condition that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution, and a guanfacine arm: under the same condition that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution, guanfacine retains residual working memory/attention phenotype ≥50% of guanfacine-alone (WM/attention units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified) — assumption-kill / alpha2-insufficiency.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Why It Matters
content_blocks.content: Guanfacine PFC working-memory/attention phenotypes are commonly framed as alpha2A orthosteric agonism. Franowicz young-rhesus and Decamp aged-NHP are phenotype priors without a residual-under-abolish arm. Franowicz alpha2A mutation and Avery idazoxan/MK912 reverse are necessity AGAINST residual. N23 asks whether residual guanfacine WM/attention phenotype survives an alpha2A LOF or alpha2-antagonist match that kills alpha2-class PFC WM attribution — alpha2-insufficiency assumption-kill. Distinct from N15–N22 (modafinil×DAT, creatine, Hericium×NGF/TrkA, L-theanine×adenosine, Rhodiola×HPA/cortisol, Bacopa×AChE, nicotine×nAChR, tyrosine×AMPT).

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Alpha2-insufficiency assumption-kill: guanfacine moves PFC delayed-response/delayed-alternation/attention phenotypes, and alpha2A genetic LOF or alpha2 antagonists (idazoxan/MK912) can frame alpha2-class WM necessity (mutation annuls guanfacine enhancement; idazoxan/MK912 reverse guanfacine spatial WM). No published head-to-head scores residual-positive guanfacine WM/attention under an alpha2A LOF or antagonist match that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution on the same panel as a retained residual. Preferred assay: same-panel acute/subacute PFC WM/attention lock (named published Franowicz/Avery-class rodent delayed-alternation or NHP delayed-response/spatial WM panel) with alpha2-class positive WM ± alpha2A LOF or named alpha2-antagonist-matched abolish condition vs guanfacine ± same condition.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references identified:
1. PMID 12351753 (Franowicz/Arnsten, J Neurosci 2002): alpha2A-AR point-mutation functional KO impairs T-maze delayed-alternation WM and annuls guanfacine cognitive enhancement — necessity AGAINST residual under alpha2A LOF.
2. PMID 12122489 (Avery/Arnsten, Psychopharmacology 2002): idazoxan and MK912 dose-dependently reverse guanfacine-induced spatial WM improvement in rhesus — pharmacological necessity AGAINST residual under antagonist match.
3. PMID 9537677 (Franowicz/Arnsten, Psychopharmacology 1998): guanfacine improves delayed-response performance in young adult rhesus — phenotype prior; no alpha2-abolish residual arm.
4. PMID 21883531 (Decamp, Eur J Neurosci 2011): guanfacine improves attention/WM in aged NHP — phenotype prior; no alpha2-abolish residual arm.
PRIOR_ART status: PARTIAL — necessity AGAINST residual FOUND; residual-positive under abolish ABSENT.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Under alpha2A genetic LOF or alpha2-antagonist match that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution, guanfacine still retains WM or attention phenotype on the same panel — OR Franowicz 12351753/Avery 12122489 already prove residual under abolish — OR Franowicz/Decamp phenotype already constitutes residual-under-abolish H2H — OR N15–N22 already settle residual guanfacine under alpha2 abolish.

Baseline measured: Franowicz alpha2A mutation annuls guanfacine delayed-alternation enhancement — necessity AGAINST residual (PMID 12351753). Avery idazoxan/MK912 reverse guanfacine spatial-WM — necessity AGAINST residual (PMID 12122489). Franowicz young-rhesus delayed-response phenotype (PMID 9537677). Decamp aged-NHP attention/WM phenotype (PMID 21883531). Matched residual-positive guanfacine under alpha2A LOF or antagonist match — UNKNOWN. Residual guanfacine phenotype ≥50% of guanfacine-alone when alpha2-class PFC WM attribution abolished — PREDICTION.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N1–N22 as proving N23 — each prior experiment (N15 modafinil/DAT, N16 plasma-Cr/PCr, N17 Hericium/NGF/TrkA, N18 theanine-adenosine, N19 Rhodiola-HPA, N20 Bacopa-AChE, N21 nicotine-nAChR, N22 tyrosine-AMPT) is distinct; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual gain.
2. Necessity AGAINST residual FOUND (Franowicz 12351753 genetic annul; Avery 12122489 idazoxan/MK912 reverse) — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL OK, not auto-REJECT; do not invent residual-positive H2H from necessity literature. Phenotype ≠ residual — Franowicz 9537677/Decamp 21883531 lack abolish residual arms. Adjacent Nishitomi 29476896 alpha2A-antagonist block of guanfacine impulsive-choice is wrong primary endpoint for WM residual.
3. Lock same-panel acute/subacute PFC WM/attention assay (prefer named published Franowicz/Avery-class rodent delayed-alternation or NHP delayed-response/spatial WM); optional cell/SPR/alpha2A occupancy overlay only after abolish×residual locks; no dosing; NOT MB/MAOI; not N15–N22 clones; do not burn ip_class=none.

content_blocks.title: Refute Condition
content_blocks.content: On the pre-registered acute/subacute PFC working memory/attention panel, under alpha2A genetic LOF or an alpha2-antagonist-matched condition that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution, residual guanfacine working memory/attention phenotype falls below 50% of guanfacine-alone (WM/attention units as pre-specified) — so alpha2-class sufficiency for the guanfacine phenotype survives and alpha2-insufficiency fails — when abolish-gate, guanfacine-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts that would otherwise leave the test inconclusive are ruled out.

key_findings: N23 is a proposed (NOT_RUN) assumption-kill experiment testing whether guanfacine retains ≥50% of its WM/attention phenotype when alpha2A-class PFC WM attribution is abolished via genetic LOF or pharmacological antagonism.

Necessity AGAINST residual is established in the literature: Franowicz/Arnsten (PMID 12351753) showed alpha2A-AR point-mutation functional KO annuls guanfacine cognitive enhancement in T-maze delayed-alternation; Avery/Arnsten (PMID 12122489) showed idazoxan and MK912 dose-dependently reverse guanfacine-induced spatial WM improvement in rhesus.
Phenotype priors exist (Franowicz PMID 9537677; Decamp PMID 21883531) but lack abolish residual arms — phenotype ≠ residual.
The key variable — matched residual-positive guanfacine under alpha2A LOF or antagonist match that abolishes alpha2-class PFC WM attribution — is UNKNOWN; no published H2H result found.
PRIOR_ART status: PARTIAL — necessity AGAINST residual FOUND; residual-positive under abolish ABSENT.

Preferred assay design: same-panel acute/subacute PFC WM/attention (Franowicz/Avery-class rodent delayed-alternation or NHP delayed-response/spatial WM) with alpha2-class positive WM arm ± alpha2A LOF or named alpha2-antagonist-matched abolish condition vs guanfacine ± same condition.

Competing caveats that would render test inconclusive (not refuted): abolish condition fails to kill alpha2-class PFC WM attribution, guanfacine-alone null, underpowered strata, assay-identity mismatch.
Execution status: NOT_RUN; kill cost tier 2; estimated time to refute: 6 weeks.

N23 is distinct from N15 (modafinil×DAT), N16 (creatine/PCr), N17 (Hericium×NGF/TrkA), N18 (theanine×adenosine), N19 (Rhodiola×HPA/cortisol), N20 (Bacopa×AChE), N21 (nicotine×nAChR), N22 (tyrosine×AMPT); alpha2 antagonism ≠ AMPT catecholamine depletion.
